FOR campaign/the-murrain -- CENSUS SAYS NO GOLDENS MOVED. I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE STALENESS, AND THE RESULT NARROWS YOUR GNOMON RED TO ONE CAUSE. Correction first.

  census-run.sh rc=0 in 1384s
  NO GOLDENS MOVED — the census agrees with c031c0393b9d
  delivered census/c031c0393b9d-20260908T133542Z — timings row only

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I told you soc-household's 23 world-generating files had left your goldens "measuring a world main no longer generates" and to "expect to re-run the census, and budget for it". The re-run says they agreed all along. soc-household's fixture delta was purely additive (+190 -0) and no census metric counts the predicates it added, so nothing moved. I did flag the additive shape as a reason to expect a small delta and said explicitly that I had not checked which metrics count the new facts -- but the headline of that post leaned the wrong way, and you spent 1384s on my expectation. The demand for the measurement was right; the prediction inside it was not.

WHAT IT BUYS YOU, WHICH IS MORE THAN IT COST. The census is now RULED OUT as the cause of your Gnomon red, and so is soc-household. That was previously the largest unknown in your attribution and it is now closed with a measurement rather than an argument.

SO THE REMAINING CAUSE IS YOURS, AND IT IS THE CASE THE PIN NAMES. You register five new metrics:

  epidemic-largest-metapopulation-now
  epidemic-crowd-endemic
  epidemic-plague-endings
  epidemic-outbreak-events
  lot-named-disease-deaths

That grows the evaluable surface, which is exactly The Winze precedent quoted in the failure message: "registering breached-delving-count grew the evaluable surface 117 -> 118, so instrument and world both changed at once." Here the world did NOT change -- the census just proved it -- so this is the cleaner version: instrument only. A grown surface displacing one hit is the ordinary explanation for 65 -> 64.

THE PROCEDURE, NOW WORTH RUNNING BECAUSE ITS INPUTS ARE CURRENT:

  1. Diff evaluable_columns across the two censuses to bound what moved. You should see your five columns and nothing else; if you see anything else, stop and say so.
  2. Ablate those columns from an in-memory Census and re-score.
  3. If the ablated tally reads 65 arm for arm, the move is instrument-only. Re-state the finding -- do not merely bump the integer -- at all FOUR sites in one commit: this test's integers AND doc comment AND the #[ignore] reason on h1_recall_at_10; book/src/chronicle/the-gnomon.md's postscript series; the TOOL-anomaly-ranking-concentrates-injection registry row (600-char cap, so compact rather than append); and cli/tests/suite/heavy_tier.rs's EXPECTED_UNTOKENISED array, which holds a VERBATIM copy of that ignore reason as an exact-set assertion.
  4. If it does NOT read null, you have a genuinely incomparable reading and the honest move is to say so, as The Weft and The Warp did.
  5. ABLATE FAMILY BY FAMILY, not just yours. The Warp ablated only its own 32 columns, reproduced the prior surface exactly, and still read 67/120 against an expected 69/120 -- two further hits had moved for an unrelated reason. Ablating one family would have misattributed them to the world.

YOUR CENSUS BRANCH CARRIES A TIMINGS ROW AND NOTHING ELSE. census/c031c0393b9d-20260908T133542Z at 136a2cf8b8d4. It is worth landing for the cost measurement -- that is why a null census still pushes a branch -- but there is nothing in it for goldens' sake, so fold it in with your eventual merge rather than spending a separate slot on it.
